c.tagline: Tanzania's safari capital - gateway to the Serengeti, Ngorongoro and Kilimanjaro.

taxi.color: white or unmarked sedans (no uniform colour)
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered - agree the fare before the ride. App-based Bolt, Uber and Yango offer prepaid pricing in the city, though coverage is thinner than in Dar es Salaam.

emergency.note: 112 is the general emergency number reaching police, fire and ambulance; 114 also reaches police. Private clinics such as Arusha Lutheran Medical Centre and AICC Hospital serve travelers, and flying-doctor evacuation covers the safari areas.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: fine by day; extra caution after dark

avoid.reason: Touts and petty crime around the bus stand and curio shops; caution at night

hood_desc: Downtown Arusha around the landmark Clock Tower, packed with safari operators, curio shops, cafes and the Central Market; the convenient walkable base where most first-timers stay before or after a safari.
A leafy, upscale southeastern suburb with the Njiro Complex mall, restaurants, bars and gated communities; the go-to area for dining and nightlife.
A green residential area east of the centre near the Themi River, lined with guesthouses, boutique hotels and gardens; quiet yet close to town.
The northwestern gateway suburb along the Nairobi-Moshi road with views of Mount Meru, hotels and the nearby Maasai and curio markets; a handy arrival/departure base.
A green, semi-rural area ~20 km east toward the airport and Arusha National Park, dotted with coffee estates, gardens and country lodges; peaceful and scenic.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only; tap water is not potable.

transit.pay: Dala-dala fares are paid in cash to the conductor on board; bajaji (auto-rickshaw) and boda-boda (motorbike) fares are negotiated. There is no fare card system, so most visitors use taxis or ride-hailing apps (Bolt, Uber, Yango) instead.
transit.hours: Dala-dalas run roughly 6am-9pm and thin out after dark; use a taxi or ride-hail app at night.
transit.note: Arusha has no metro or rail; locals get around on crowded dala-dala minibuses, three-wheeled bajaji and boda-boda motorbike taxis. The compact centre is walkable, and most visitors combine walking with taxis or ride-hailing apps.

bus: Intercity coaches to Moshi, Dar es Salaam and Dodoma

transit.m: Kilimanjaro Air Bus shuttle to Arusha (~1 hr)

tip.r: Tipping is customary in the safari sector - roughly $20-30/day for safari guides and $10-15/day for cook and camp staff; ~10% at restaurants is appreciated.

food.desc: Goat or beef roasted slowly over charcoal, chopped on a board and eaten by hand with kachumbari salad, chilli and a mound of ugali.

places.name: The Blue Heron

food.name: Ugali with mboga
food.desc: Stiff maize-meal staple pinched into a scoop and dipped in beans, mchicha greens, beef stew or grilled meat juices; the everyday plate.

places.name: Central Market mama ntilie
places.note: Informal cooked-food stalls serving home-style ugali plates at local prices.

places.name: Kilombero Market

places.name: The Blue Heron
places.note: Comfortable garden setting for a first, gently introduced ugali plate.

food.name: Mishkaki
food.desc: Cubes of beef or goat marinated in ginger, garlic and chilli, threaded on skewers and grilled over charcoal at roadside braziers after dark.

places.name: Khan's BBQ

food.name: Chipsi mayai
food.desc: Tanzania's chip omelette: hot chips folded into beaten egg and set in a pan, cut into wedges and doused with kachumbari and chilli sauce.

places.name: Africafe

food.name: Mtori
food.desc: Chagga soup from the Kilimanjaro slopes: green cooking bananas simmered with beef and mashed to a thick, smoky broth; a breakfast and recovery dish.

places.name: Central Market mama ntilie

food.name: Tanzanian coffee
food.desc: Arabica grown on the volcanic slopes of Meru and Kilimanjaro, roasted locally and served black or as a milky spiced cup with breakfast.

places.name: Africafe
places.note: Long-running cafe roasting and pouring locally grown beans in the town centre.

places.name: Arusha Coffee Lodge

places.name: Fifi's

places.name: Uzunguni City Park

places.name: The Blue Heron

landmarks: Arusha National Park and Mount Meru
Tanzania's most underrated park sits on the city's doorstep, where giraffes graze beneath Mount Meru's 4,566-metre volcanic spire.
Arusha Clock Tower
The city's famous roundabout landmark, popularly said to mark the midpoint between Cairo and Cape Town on Africa's great overland route.
Cultural Heritage Centre
A spiralling gallery complex showcasing East African art, Makonde carvings, tanzanite jewellery, and one of Africa's largest curio collections.
Maasai Market (Curio Market)
A vibrant warren of stalls piled with beadwork, tinga tinga paintings, kangas, and carvings, perfect for haggling before or after safari.
Old Boma Museum
Arusha's oldest building, an 1886 German fortified administrative post now housing a natural history museum on human evolution and colonial history.
Lake Duluti
A tranquil forest-rimmed crater lake just outside town, circled by a walking trail alive with kingfishers, monitor lizards, and canoeists.
Ngurdoto Crater
A flooded-forest 'little Ngorongoro' within Arusha National Park, its three-kilometre-wide caldera floor roamed by buffalo and warthog below rim viewpoints.
Momella Lakes
A chain of shallow alkaline lakes in Arusha National Park, each a different hue and seasonally tinged pink with flocks of flamingos.
The Tanzanite Experience Museum
An engaging city-centre museum telling the story of tanzanite, the violet-blue gemstone found only in the Mererani Hills near Arusha.
Shanga Workshop
An inspiring social enterprise at Arusha Coffee Lodge where artisans with disabilities blow recycled glass and weave beadwork before visitors' eyes.

train.note: Arusha has no working passenger railway - the old branch from Moshi carries no scheduled service, and Tanzania's new SGR network (https://www.trc.co.tz/) runs from Dar es Salaam toward Dodoma and Mwanza, well to the south. Arrive by coach or fly into Kilimanjaro International Airport, about an hour east.

intl.to: Nairobi (Kenya) - via the Namanga border, ~5-6 hr
intl.op: Riverside Shuttle / Impala Shuttle — tickets through Arusha travel agents

bus.note: Arusha is the main overland link between northern Tanzania and Kenya. The Nairobi shuttles are minibuses aimed at travellers and take five to six hours including the Namanga border, where you clear both countries - carry your passport and note that Tanzania needs its own visa, separate from the East Africa Tourist Visa. Domestic coaches to Dar es Salaam take 8-10 hours and Moshi about 90 minutes.

ferry.note: Arusha is inland at the foot of Mount Meru with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. Lake Victoria's boats operate from Mwanza, a long day's drive west, and the Zanzibar catamarans sail from Dar es Salaam.

half.name: Arusha National Park
half.blurb: Compact park ~25 km east with Mount Meru, the Momella Lakes, giraffe, colobus monkeys and walking/canoe safaris.

full.name: Ngorongoro Crater
full.blurb: The world's largest intact volcanic caldera ~180 km west, a UNESCO site teeming with lions, rhino, elephant and flamingos.

full.name: Lake Manyara National Park
full.blurb: Rift Valley park ~120 km west known for tree-climbing lions, huge elephant herds and flamingo-lined shores.

full.name: Tarangire National Park
full.blurb: Baobab-studded park ~120 km southwest famous for its enormous elephant populations along the Tarangire River.
